method: Direct visual inspection of all 24 primary PNGs, 5 diagnostics and the manifest. Full-page primaries were additionally re-cropped at native resolution (Pillow crop/stack, no resampling) to defeat Read-tool downsampling: pricing plan cards y330-720, pricing logo strip y1060-1320, pricing table header y1420-1520, pricing Support band y4680-4930, changelog bands y430-1010 / y1100-2000 / y2600-3500 / y6000-6900, security hero y140-420, security feature grid y600-1200, security marquee y2350-2750, stripe hero y0-720 and stripe stat/testimonial bands. Metric JSON was used only as secondary context and, once, to LOCATE candidate regression bands (500px-band @16 sweep of source-vs-old against source-vs-hardened on all three linear routes) which were then judged by eye.

observations: ICON CONTRAST - the headline fix. In the OLD build every check/cross glyph in both the plan cards and the comparison table is painted as a near-black disc on the near-black panel: at native resolution the plan-card bullets are effectively invisible and the table's cross glyphs are absent. In the HARDENED build they render as crisp white filled check discs and visible grey crosses, matching the source glyph-for-glyph. diagnostic-01 shows this directly and the same band goes from almost-solid red in OLD DIFF to nearly clean in HARDENED DIFF.

LOGO STRIP OVERLAP COLLAPSE FIXED - the single most dramatic change. In OLD the 'Trusted by more than 40,000 companies' marquee is a pile-up: nine wordmarks (Vercel / CURSOR / OSCAR / OpenAI / coinbase / Cash App / BOOM / ramp) crushed into one overlapping cluster roughly 700px wide, letterforms physically colliding. HARDENED reproduces the source exactly: seven evenly spaced logos (OpenAI, Vercel, salesforce, Figma, CURSOR, coinbase, ramp) on the same x-positions as the live page.
The old build's 12px vertical shortfall is gone (heightDelta -12 -> 0); the 'Core' heading and all subsequent rows now sit at the source's y.

In the OLD DIFF the entire comparison table is a stack of solid red blocks section by section (Core, AI and agent workflows, Integrations, Team management, Analytics, Linear Asks, Security, Support). In the HARDENED DIFF every one of those blocks is gone; the only remaining saturated area is the single 'Features | Free | Basic | Business | Enterprise' header band.

RESIDUAL - header-row font weight. At native resolution the source renders the header row in a regular weight with open tracking; the hardened build renders it noticeably bolder and tighter. Same typeface and same glyph shapes (no substitution), wrong weight. This is what keeps that one band solid red.

RESIDUAL, NOT A REGRESSION - the Basic/Business card price reads 'US$10 / US$16 per user/month' in the source and '$10 / $16 per user/month' in BOTH the old and the hardened clone. The currency prefix is dropped identically in both builds, so 28.5B neither caused nor fixed it. Consistent with a locale/geo-resolved currency string.

Remaining red on body labels and the Support-section glyphs in the hardened diff is hairline anti-alias edging (the diff is rendered at the >=1/255 threshold); side by side those rows are indistinguishable from the source.
No new overlaps, no new clipping, no column collapse, no missing media, no empty space introduced anywhere on this route.

B.verdictCaveat: Improved overall and far beyond what the @16 delta of -0.0054 suggests, but this group carries the pack's one genuine old-vs-hardened visual regression (the first video's rendered frame).
observations: The metric badly understates this route. At native resolution the OLD build is structurally broken over most of the page and the HARDENED build is not. At y2600-3500 the OLD clone collapses the 'Fixes / Improvements / Keyboard shortcuts' accordion into a one-character-wide column - the words render vertically, one letter per line - and that column then overlaps the 'Team initiatives' heading. HARDENED reproduces the source's three full-width rows with chevrons exactly.

OLD's entry body column is roughly half the source's width, so every paragraph overflows its box and paragraphs physically collide with each other (verified at y1100-2000 and y6000-6900: 'During a session, Linear detects...' overprints the paragraph above it; 'Support for GitHub teams in reviews' overprints its own body). HARDENED matches the source line-for-line with identical wrap points and zero collisions.

OLD wraps the first entry heading as four narrow lines ('Coding sessions: / environments, / browser use, and / updated pricing') and the date column as three ('August / 20, / 2026'). HARDENED matches the source: two-line heading, one-line date.

REGRESSION (local, video only) - image 12 / diagnostic-05 / native crop y430-1010. The source's embedded video shows its poster frame: three stacked panels labelled 'Go backend', 'Data service', 'Web app', timer 00:00, empty scrubber. The OLD clone reproduces that frame closely. The HARDENED clone shows a DIFFERENT frame entirely: a single dark tilted 'Web app' card on a mostly black field, with a partly advanced scrubber and stray 'Agent' text sitting on the control bar. The video element itself is present and its box geometry is pixel-correct in all three - this is a wrong frame / playback-position mismatch, not missing media. The diffs corroborate: OLD DIFF leaves the poster largely visible through the wash, HARDENED DIFF paints the whole poster solid red.

That video band is the ONLY place on this 25,342px page where hardened is worse than old. A 500px-band sweep across the full page found exactly one band (y500-1000, old 1.17% -> hardened 6.91% at >=16/255); every other band is equal or better.
Residual present in BOTH builds: +1px page height vs source, unchanged by 28.5B, and body-text anti-alias edging that keeps the diff pink over paragraphs.
No column collapse, no empty space and no overlaps remain in the hardened build; all three were present in old.

HERO LINE BREAK FIXED and it is unmistakable at native resolution. SOURCE breaks 'Safe, secure, / and private.'; the OLD build breaks 'Safe, secure, and / private.'; the HARDENED build breaks 'Safe, secure, / and private.' - matching the source. Image 16 (old diff) shows the headline as an unreadable double exposure of two different line arrangements; image 17 (hardened diff) shows a clean two-line ghost.

FEATURE-CARD ICONS RESTORED - not called out in the manifest but clearly visible at y600-1200. The OLD build is missing every small feature glyph (the SOC 2, GDPR, HIPAA, ISO 27001, App approvals, Audit logs and Admin controls marks, and the lock before the 'Enterprise-grade security' eyebrow). HARDENED paints all of them at source weight and position. Same root symptom as the /pricing glyph field.
Footer content drift also resolved: OLD's Product column reads 'Intake / Plan / Build / Beta / Pricing / Security'; source and HARDENED both read 'Intake / Plan / AI / Build / Pricing / Security'.

RESIDUAL - headline weight and tracking. The hardened headline is visibly heavier and tighter than the source's; measured across 'Safe, secure,' the hardened line is a few px narrower. Typeface and glyph shapes are correct - this is weight/tracking, not font substitution or bad rasterization. It is what makes the diff a ghosted double image rather than clean. The same too-heavy rendering shows on the 'Plan the present. Build the future.' CTA line.

RESIDUAL, unchanged from old - the two-line sub-headline still wraps at the wrong word: source '...safe and secure. / Because your business is nobody else's business.' vs clone '...safe and secure. Because / your business is nobody else's business.'

RESIDUAL present in BOTH builds - the left intro column ('Peace of mind-as-a-service...') is wider in both clones than in the source, so that paragraph sets in 5 wide lines instead of the source's 4 narrow ones. Not caused and not fixed by 28.5B.
The customer logo marquee sits at a different animation phase in both clones; content is identical, phase is not. Cosmetic, present in both.
No new overlaps, clipping, collapsed columns, empty space or missing media. A 200px-band sweep found no band where hardened is worse than old anywhere on this route.

responsive.question: does the hardened clone at 700/1100 match source?
responsive.verdict: NO - does not match; confirmed known defect, not new and not worse
observations: At 1100px (images 21/22, diagnostic-02) the defect is exactly as documented. The source has reflowed to 1100 and shows the full comparison table: header row 'Features | Free | Basic | Business | Enterprise' plus four populated value columns. The clone shows NO header row and only the first value column ('Unlimited / 10MB / 250 issues / 2 teams'); the space where Basic, Business and Enterprise belong is empty page background - genuine content disappearance, not merely off-canvas.

Same root cause, additionally visible in the full-page image 22 and worth recording: at 1100 the clone is serving its 1440 variant unreflowed, so the right ~340px is clipped off-canvas. The nav truncates mid-word at 'Cont', the Enterprise plan card survives only as a sliver at the right edge, the logo strip cuts mid-word at 'coin', the footer's 'Connect' column is gone and the bottom CTA is centred on 1440 so it sits visibly right of centre. This is the same 'only 390 and 1440 were observed' cause the manifest names in diagnostic-03; it is a fuller description of the known defect, not a different or worse one.

At 914px (diagnostic-03) confirmed as described: the clone serves the 390 variant, content stays locked in a ~390px column with roughly 55% of the canvas empty, and the nav is a hamburger where the source shows the full desktop bar with two plan cards side by side.

At 700px (images 19/20) the defect is milder because the source is also single-column at this width. Both are stacked Free/Basic/Business/Enterprise and all content is present in the clone. The visible tells are the footer grid (source 3 columns per band, clone 2) and marquee phase, plus the -81px height shortfall.

Judged against the manifest's description: this is the SAME defect, same mechanism, same direction. Nothing new, nothing worse, no content loss beyond the header row and three value columns already documented.

secondSite.route: stripe.com root desktop 1440 (images 23/24, diagnostic-04 as context)
secondSite.verdict: materially improved is not assessable (no old counterpart exists); as an absolute fidelity judgement: GOOD STRUCTURE, THREE CLEARLY VISIBLE DEFECTS
observations: Generalisation off linear.app is real. Section order, section count, page height (heightDelta 0), the navy 'The backbone of global commerce' band with its photographic stripe-sessions banner, the customer-logo bands, the long dark integration section and the full footer all reproduce closely; several bands are essentially indistinguishable at native resolution.

DEFECT 1, missing media - the hero's animated aurora gradient is entirely absent. In the source it fills the top-right two-fifths of the hero with an orange/pink/violet mesh; in the clone that area is blank white. This is the largest single visible difference on the page and is almost certainly the WebGL/canvas hero.

DEFECT 2, background-clip:text painted as a solid block. The '500M+ / 10K+ / 150K+' statistics are gradient-filled TEXT in the source (glyph-clipped, navy showing between the letters). The clone paints the gradient as an opaque rectangle behind each number, so they read as pale text sitting inside bright pink and violet swatches. The trailing '+' is lost from '10K+' and '150K+' and reappears displaced as a stray white glyph overlapping the caption text below ('API requests per second', 'transactions per minute') - a new overlap and a clipping artifact in the same element.

DEFECT 3, low-contrast nav control - the source's 'Sign in' is a white pill with a border and a coloured label; the clone renders it as faint grey text with no pill and no border, barely legible against white.

Lesser residuals: several containers are narrower than the source, so the hero paragraph breaks at a different word, the testimonial attribution wraps onto two lines and the 'Read the story' link wraps into two lines; and the selected customer-tab logo ('mindbody') stays grey in the clone instead of switching to the active dark treatment, although its purple underline is drawn.

diagnostic-04 (media-entertainment, mobile) is as described: all copy present, the clone's larger horizontal insets and line-height make every text block taller and the offset accumulates to +924px. Box metrics, not content loss.

defectChecklist.fontShape: No wrong-typeface substitution and no bad rasterization seen anywhere. Glyph shapes match the source on all four sites/routes. The real typographic defect is WEIGHT and TRACKING: the hardened build renders the /security hero, the /security CTA line and the /pricing table header row heavier and tighter than the source. Present in the old build too; unchanged by hardening.
defectChecklist.wrapping: Materially improved. /security hero break fixed ('Safe, secure, and / private.' -> 'Safe, secure, / and private.'). /changelog headings, dates and every body paragraph now wrap exactly like the source where old wrapped into a half-width column. Two wrap residuals remain, both identical in old and hardened: the /security sub-headline breaks one word late, and the /security left intro column is wider than the source's. On stripe, several containers are narrower than the source so the hero paragraph, the testimonial attribution and the 'Read the story' link all break differently.
defectChecklist.pseudoMismatch: Old build painted decorations at near-zero contrast or not at all: /pricing check and cross glyphs invisible, /security feature-card icons and the eyebrow lock entirely missing. Hardened paints all of them correctly - no case found of the hardened build painting a decoration that should not be there on the linear routes. The one paint-that-should-not-be-there in the pack is on stripe: the background-clip:text gradient on the 500M+/10K+/150K+ statistics is rendered as an opaque gradient rectangle instead of being clipped to the glyphs.
defectChecklist.iconContrast: This is the pack's clearest win. /pricing plan-card bullets and table check/cross glyphs go from effectively invisible (dark disc on dark panel) to source-weight white; /security feature-card marks go from absent to present. Only remaining contrast fault is on stripe: the 'Sign in' control loses its pill and border and its label is barely legible.
defectChecklist.missingMedia: Two findings. (1) /changelog: the video ELEMENT is present and pixel-correctly boxed, but the hardened build captures a different frame than the source (dark 'Web app' frame with an advanced scrubber vs the source's three-panel poster at 00:00) - and the OLD build got this right, so it is a local regression. (2) stripe.com hero: the animated aurora gradient artwork is entirely absent, leaving blank white. No missing media on /pricing or /security.
defectChecklist.columnCollapse: Old /changelog had severe collapse - accordion rows collapsed to a one-character-wide column and the entry body column to roughly half width - and the hardened build fixes both completely. The only column loss remaining is the known responsive one: at 1100px the clone's comparison table loses its header row and three of four value columns.
defectChecklist.emptySpace: No new empty space at desktop widths. Empty space is confined to the known responsive defect: at 914px roughly 55% of the canvas is blank beside a 390px-locked column, and at 1100px the Basic/Business/Enterprise columns are blank page background. On stripe, the missing hero gradient leaves the top-right of the hero blank white.
defectChecklist.responsiveDisappearance: Confirmed and matching the documented defect. At 1100px the clone loses the comparison-table header row and three of four value columns (~286 characters), and additionally clips the right ~340px of a 1440-wide layout (nav truncated at 'Cont', Enterprise card reduced to a sliver, logo strip cut mid-word, footer 'Connect' column gone). At 914px the 390 variant is served. At 700px all content is present and only the footer grid and page height differ. Same defect, same mechanism, not new and not worse than described.
defectChecklist.newOverlaps: None introduced on the linear routes - the reverse: the old build's overlaps (the /pricing logo-strip pile-up and the /changelog paragraph and heading collisions) are all gone in hardened. Two overlaps do exist in hardened output: stray 'Agent' text over the /changelog video's control bar, and the displaced '+' glyphs overprinting the stripe statistic captions.
defectChecklist.newClipping: No new clipping on the linear desktop routes. Clipping seen is (a) the known responsive defect's right-edge cut of the 1440 layout at 1100px and (b) on stripe, the '+' clipped out of the '10K+'/'150K+' gradient boxes and the 'Read the story' link forced to wrap in a too-narrow container.

newBlockerRegressions.severity: minor-blocker candidate - localized, non-structural, but the hardened build is genuinely worse than the old build here
newBlockerRegressions.whatISaw: The source video shows its poster frame - three stacked panels labelled 'Go backend', 'Data service', 'Web app', timer 00:00, empty scrubber. The OLD clone reproduces that frame closely. The HARDENED clone shows a different frame: a single dark tilted 'Web app' card on a mostly black field, with a partly advanced scrubber and stray 'Agent' text on the control bar. Box geometry is identical in all three, so the element and its layout are correct - only the rendered frame is wrong.
newBlockerRegressions.scope: This is the single 500px band, out of 51 spanning the whole 25,342px page, where hardened measures worse than old (1.17% -> 6.91% at >=16/255). Equivalent band sweeps over /pricing and /security found no band where hardened is worse than old at a +0.5pp threshold.
newBlockerRegressions.likelyCause: non-deterministic video playback position at capture time rather than a layout or paint change; worth confirming whether the capture path pauses and seeks video to 0 before screenshotting.

notes: Overall: three of four groups are materially improved, and in two of them (changelog layout, security feature icons) the improvement is far larger than the reported @16 delta implies - the changelog in particular goes from structurally broken (one-character-wide accordion column, colliding paragraphs) to source-matching, while its headline metric moved only -0.0054, because text occupies a small share of a 36-megapixel page. The responsive group is the documented, deliberately unfixed defect and I confirm it is the same defect, unchanged in kind and degree. Exactly one old-vs-hardened regression was found in the entire pack (the /changelog video frame) and it is localized, non-structural and probably a capture-determinism issue rather than a pipeline change. The stripe pair shows the pipeline genuinely generalises off linear.app on structure and height, with three clearly visible fidelity defects of its own (missing WebGL hero gradient, background-clip:text rendered as opaque blocks with displaced '+' glyphs, low-contrast 'Sign in' control) - none of which can be called regressions since no old stripe build exists. I did not verify any claim by reading source code or QA JSON beyond the manifest; all findings above are from the images.
